{{Quote|They say any woman who can survive a plate of ''tiingilar'' is a keeper.|[[Torian Cadera]]|<ref name="TOR">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''</ref>
}}
'''''Tiingilar''''' was an intensely [[Spice/Legends|spicy]] casserole made by members of the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] culture, using a blend of meat, [[Vegetable/Legends|vegetables]], and potent spices. ''Tiingilar''{{'s}} spices gave the dish a pungent scent, enough to burn an individual's [[Nose/Legends|nasal]] passages. This effect was known as ''hetikles'',<ref name="O66" /> or "noseburn," when translated from the [[Mando'a/Legends|''Mando'a'']] [[Language/Legends|language]] to [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Galactic Basic Standard]]. Prized by Mandalorians,<ref name="Mando'a">{{WebCite|url=http://www.karentraviss.com/page20/page26/index.html|text=Mando'a|author=Karen Traviss|work=[http://www.karentraviss.com Karen Traviss]|archivedate=20110925083955}}</ref> it was one of four qualities sought after in Mandalorian cooking,<ref name="O66" /> and made ''tiingilar'' a favored dish of many Mandalorians.<ref name="TOR" />

Shortly after the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic's]] [[Declaration of a New Order|transformation]] into the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], a large bowl of ''tiingilar'' was served during a family dinner at the [[Clan Skirata|Skirata clan's]] [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]] [[Kyrimorut/Legends|residence]]. The [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]]-turned-Mandalorian, [[Bardan Jusik]], used the dish in a [[Telekinesis/Legends|demonstration]] of casual [[Force power/Legends|Force usage]] for a young [[Venku Skirata]], before the ''tiingilar'' was eventually eaten by the other individuals in attendance.<ref name="O66" />

==Behind the scenes==
''Tiingilar'' first appeared in the ''[[Republic Commando]]'' novel, [[Order 66: A Republic Commando Novel|''Order 66'']], written by [[Karen Traviss]] and published in [[2008]].<ref name="O66" />
